s01-i00.text: This is the moment Anthropic became the biggest IPO in history.

s01-i01.text: The maker of Claude raised 93.5 billion dollars, more than any company had ever raised in a stock market debut.

s01-i02.text: Its shares opened at 111 dollars and 50 cents, 34 percent above the price set the night before.

s01-i03.text: And one day later, more than half of that first-day gain was gone.

s01-i04.text: So what happened? Let's go back to the start.

s02-i00.text: Anthropic was founded in 2021 by seven people who left OpenAI.

s02-i01.text: Dario Amodei became chief executive. His sister Daniela became president.

s02-i02.text: The other five co-founders are Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish and Chris Olah.

s02-i03.text: Their company makes Claude, a family of AI models that first launched in 2023.

s02-i04.text: And Claude has grown fast. In the first nine months of 2026, Anthropic's revenue was 33.24 billion dollars, about 13 times as much as a year earlier.

s02-i05.text: In the third quarter alone, it was about 17 billion dollars.

s02-i06.text: On paper, it still lost 104 billion dollars in those nine months. But most of that was an accounting charge: its convertible notes became worth more as the company did. The business itself lost about 1.3 billion dollars.

s02-i07.text: At Nasdaq, Daniela Amodei put it bluntly.

s02-i09.text: Part of that is written into its legal structure. Anthropic is a public benefit corporation.

s02-i10.text: By law, it has to weigh its shareholders against its mission: the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.

s02-i11.text: Even after the listing, the seven co-founders keep 50.1 percent of the votes, through a special entity called Founder LLC.

s02-i12.text: That matters, because from now on outside shareholders own most of the company.

s03-i00.text: On the 10th of November, Anthropic started its roadshow, the meetings where the banks pitch a new stock to big investors.

s03-i01.text: The plan was to sell 825 million shares at 70 to 78 dollars each.

s03-i02.text: But demand was so strong that the plan changed.

s03-i03.text: On the 18th of November, Anthropic priced its shares at 83 dollars, above the top of the range.

s03-i04.text: And instead of 825 million shares, it sold 980 million.

s03-i05.text: Raising the price and the number of shares at the same time is a clear sign that the banks had far more orders than shares to sell.

s03-i06.text: That first sale alone was worth 81.3 billion dollars.

s03-i07.text: The next morning, the shares would start trading on Nasdaq, under the ticker ANT.

s04-i00.text: On Thursday the 19th of November, the Nasdaq tower in Times Square was covered in Anthropic's imagery.

s04-i01.text: Down at street level, New York went about its morning.

s04-i02.text: Inside the MarketSite studio, Nasdaq's chair and chief executive, Adena Friedman, opened the ceremony.

s04-i03.text: Then Daniela Amodei took the podium.

s04-i04.text: She said more than half of the Fortune 500 now use Claude.

s04-i05.text: And she described what the company wants Claude to be.

s05-i00.text: Next came her brother, Dario Amodei.

s05-i01.text: He started with medicine, and with a big claim.

s05-i03.text: Then he turned to the risks of AI, and made a promise that investors will remember.

s05-i05.text: For a company that just sold shares to the public, that is an unusual thing to say on day one.

s05-i06.text: He closed with the line that Nasdaq later quoted in its own release.

s05-i08.text: Then the whole team walked up for the bell.

s06-i00.text: The bell rang, and Anthropic was a public company!

s06-i01.text: But the bell does not start trading in a brand new stock. The first trade in ANT only came just before noon.

s06-i02.text: And when it came, it was 111 dollars and 50 cents, 34 percent above the IPO price!

s06-i03.text: At that price, Anthropic was worth around 2 trillion dollars, fully diluted.

s06-i04.text: Fully diluted means you also count the stock the company has promised to employees, but has not handed out yet.

s06-i05.text: Counting only the shares that already exist, the value was about 1.5 trillion dollars. Still one of the most valuable companies in America, on its first morning.

s07-i00.text: So how big was this sale, really?

s07-i01.text: On the first day, the 980 million shares brought in 81.3 billion dollars.

s07-i02.text: On Friday, the banks used their option to buy 147 million extra shares, a step known as the greenshoe.

s07-i03.text: Banks normally only use that option when a new stock trades above its IPO price. And ANT did.

s07-i04.text: That lifted the total to 93.5 billion dollars.

s07-i05.text: SpaceX, the previous record holder, raised 75 billion dollars in June, and 85.7 billion with its own extra shares.

s07-i06.text: So, counted the same way, Anthropic is the new record.

s07-i07.text: And there was more. Seven technology companies bought another 26 billion dollars of a separate class of shares, at the same 83 dollars.

s07-i08.text: Together, the offering and that private sale add up to 119.5 billion dollars.

s07-i09.text: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley led the deal.

s08-i01.text: Amazon owns about 14.7 percent and Google about 13.7 percent.

s08-i02.text: Both are also major suppliers of the computing power that Anthropic runs on.

s08-i03.text: The seven co-founders each hold about 240 million shares, together about 10 percent of the company.

s08-i04.text: At the IPO price, that is roughly 20 billion dollars per founder.

s08-i05.text: And Reuters expects the listing to create thousands of paper millionaires among the staff.

s08-i06.text: Unusually, employees were allowed to sell up to 10 percent of their shares on the very first day. Most companies make their staff wait for months.

s09-i00.text: But on the trading floor, the price was already sliding.

s09-i01.text: After that opening trade, buyers who got in at 83 dollars locked in quick profits through the afternoon.

s09-i02.text: At four o'clock, Anthropic was back at Nasdaq for the closing bell.

s09-i03.text: This time chief commercial officer Paul Smith and chief financial officer Krishna Rao spoke, with some of Anthropic's customers on stage.

s09-i04.text: ANT closed its first day at 97 dollars and 17 cents.

s09-i05.text: That is still 17 percent above the IPO price. A strong first day by any normal standard.

s09-i06.text: And here is the uncomfortable side of a big first-day pop. Every share Anthropic sold at 83 dollars was worth 97 dollars by the evening.

s09-i07.text: On 980 million shares, that is roughly 14 billion dollars that went to the first buyers instead of to the company.

s09-i08.text: Fully diluted, Anthropic was now worth about 1.8 trillion dollars.

s10-i01.text: The AI trade was already nervous. Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang had just left the company, and investors were asking whether all the spending on AI would pay off.

s10-i02.text: On Friday, that fear boiled over. Nvidia fell about 14 percent, and AMD lost about 13 percent. Amazon, Google and Microsoft closed lower too.

s10-i03.text: Anthropic could not escape it. ANT fell 8.5 percent, to 88 dollars and 91 cents, close to its 83 dollar IPO price.

s10-i04.text: More than half of the first-day gain was gone in a single session.

s11-i00.text: Does that make the IPO a failure? Not for Anthropic.

s11-i01.text: The company got its money at 83 dollars a share, whatever the stock does next.

s11-i02.text: The record itself is safe for now. Remember, SpaceX held it for only five months.

s11-i03.text: And as the first frontier AI lab on the stock market, it has no direct peer to be measured against.

s11-i04.text: From now on, every quarter, ANT will show whether investors still believe in the AI boom.

s11-i05.text: So what do you think? Is this the start of something huge, or the top of the AI bubble? Tell me in the comments.
